steps.name: QC and filtering of paired count matrix
steps.question: After loading counts.csv (12000 genes x 12 samples) and metadata.csv (subject, condition for each of 4 subjects x 3 conditions), which genes pass a minimum-expression filter and do library sizes / sample correlations show any subject or condition outliers before modeling?
acceptance_criteria: Counts and metadata loaded and sample order verified to match between the two files
Low-count genes filtered (e.g., require count >=10 in at least 4 samples) with the number of genes retained reported
PCA or sample-correlation heatmap generated colored by subject and by condition to confirm subjects cluster together (paired structure) before DE modeling
Filtered count matrix and matched metadata saved for downstream DESeq2 steps

steps.name: Fit paired DESeq2 model (~subject + condition)
steps.question: Using the filtered counts and metadata with 4 subjects x {control, treated_a, treated_b}, does a paired negative-binomial model (design ~subject + condition) fit the data, and what are its dispersion/size-factor diagnostics?
acceptance_criteria: DESeq2 (R) or PyDESeq2 model fit with design formula including subject as a blocking factor and condition (control/treated_a/treated_b) as the factor of interest
Size factors and dispersion estimates reported; dispersion plot saved as diagnostic
Model object/results persisted for reuse by the three downstream contrast steps and the LRT step, avoiding refitting

steps.name: Contrast: treated_a vs control (paired)
steps.question: Which genes are significantly differentially expressed between treated_a and control, adjusting for subject as a paired covariate?
acceptance_criteria: Wald test contrast condition treated_a vs control extracted from the fitted paired model
Results table with log2FoldChange, p-value, BH-adjusted p-value (padj) for all filtered genes, saved as CSV
Significant genes reported at padj<0.05 with count and top hits listed
Volcano plot saved

steps.name: Contrast: treated_b vs control (paired)
steps.question: Which genes are significantly differentially expressed between treated_b and control, adjusting for subject as a paired covariate?
acceptance_criteria: Wald test contrast condition treated_b vs control extracted from the same fitted paired model as T1S3
Results table with log2FoldChange, p-value, padj for all filtered genes, saved as CSV
Significant genes reported at padj<0.05 with count and top hits listed
Volcano plot saved

steps.name: Contrast: treated_a vs treated_b (paired, head-to-head)
steps.question: Do the two treatments differ from each other — which genes are significantly differentially expressed between treated_a and treated_b within the same subjects?
acceptance_criteria: Wald test contrast condition treated_a vs treated_b extracted from the same fitted paired model (re-leveling condition reference to treated_b or using a contrast vector, not a refit on a data subset)
Results table with log2FoldChange, p-value, padj for all filtered genes, saved as CSV
Significant genes reported at padj<0.05 with count and top hits listed
Volcano plot saved
Explicit comparison made to T1S3/T1S4 gene lists to characterize genes shared between treatments vs unique to one treatment (e.g., Venn/UpSet overlap of the three padj<0.05 gene sets)

steps.name: Omnibus LRT: any-treatment effect within subject
steps.question: Which genes respond to either treatment at all (omnibus condition effect), testing full model ~subject + condition against reduced model ~subject only?
acceptance_criteria: Likelihood-ratio test (full ~subject+condition vs reduced ~subject) run in DESeq2/PyDESeq2 on the same filtered matrix used in T1S2
Results table with LRT stat, p-value, padj per gene saved as CSV
Genes significant at padj<0.05 reported as the 'responds to either treatment' gene set, and its overlap with the union of T1S3/T1S4 pairwise-significant genes reported as a consistency check

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of treatment-responsive and treatment-differential gene sets
steps.question: What biological pathways are enriched among genes responding to either treatment (T1S6 LRT set), among genes specific to treated_a vs control (T1S3), specific to treated_b vs control (T1S4), and among genes that differ between treated_a and treated_b (T1S5)?
acceptance_criteria: Confirm the WikiPathways human gene sets (HGNC symbols) are present in the reference store before running; if absent, report the gap and skip rather than fabricate results

Over-representation or GSEA-style enrichment run separately for: (a) LRT omnibus significant genes, (b) treated_a vs control significant genes, (c) treated_b vs control significant genes, (d) treated_a vs treated_b significant genes
Enrichment results (pathway name, WikiPathways ID, overlap genes, p-value, adjusted p-value) saved as CSV per gene set
Summary contrasting which pathways are shared across both treatments vs specific to the treated_a-vs-treated_b differential set, directly addressing whether the two treatments engage distinct biology

plan.title: Paired within-subject DE: treatment A vs B vs control (blood)
plan.analytical_narrative: Design is a repeated-measures/paired study: 4 subjects each sampled under control, treated_a, treated_b (12 samples total, 12000 genes, raw Salmon counts, single batch). The correct model is a paired multi-factor design that includes subject as a blocking covariate alongside condition, so that within-subject variance is removed from each comparison — a naive unpaired two-group test would waste power and risk confounding by subject. Track 1 runs QC/filtering once, then fits one paired DESeq2 model (~subject + condition) shared by three contrasts: treated_a vs control, treated_b vs control, and treated_a vs treated_b (the head-to-head comparison the question explicitly asks for). A likelihood-ratio test against the subject-only null additionally identifies genes responding to 'either' treatment (the omnibus condition effect), directly answering the first half of the question. Track 2 takes the three DE gene lists into pathway enrichment against WikiPathways human pathways (present in the reference store, matching organism) to give biological interpretation of what the two treatments do differently and in common. All steps operate on the actual 12-sample x 12000-gene matrix and its subject/condition metadata; no external cohort or synthetic data is used.

input.query: paired design with subject and condition covariates, multi-factor design, LRT test, contrast between two treatment levels
